subject: Post-demo: privacy / DPA clarifications and breach routing
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@medixhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@medixhealth.com
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: privacy / DPA clarifications and breach routing

Thanks for the demo earlier — really useful. A couple of follow-ups from our security/privacy review so we can line up legal and procurement: 

- High level: Medix ingests patient PII (names, dob, limited ssn tokens) and PHI-derived text. We need to confirm Redwood's role in the DPA (controller v. processor) for our use case.
- Breach notice timing: our policy requires written notification within 72 hours of confirming a breach that affects Medix data. Can Redwood commit to 72h contractual notice and provide a clear escalation contact?
- Subprocessors: please provide the current subprocessor list plus your process for notifying us of new ones and the expected notification window for additions.
- Logging/forensics: we need to understand what event logs and raw request data Redwood can provide in an incident (time range, format) and retention default. Specifically: can you export full request/response logs for a 30‑day window on-demand, and what are retention defaults?
- Data residency: requirement to keep Medix customer data in US-East only for production workloads. Is that supported and will it be included in the DPA?

Could you send a draft DPA/addendum or redline and an estimated timeline for answers? We aim to surface the DPA to procurement by early next week — if you can get materials by EOD Monday that would help.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of IT Security, Medix Health
alicia.gomez@medixhealth.com
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy / DPA clarifications and breach routing

Hi Alicia — thanks for the detailed notes and for raising these up front. Quick recap and proposed next steps below; I have attached a draft DPA and our current subprocessor list for your review.

Recap / immediate answers:
- DPA role: by default Redwood acts as a processor for customers using our hosted API. We can include explicit controller/processor mapping in the addendum to reflect your product flow.
- Breach notice: our standard target for severity-1 incidents is initial notification within 48 hours and a detailed follow-up within 72 hours. We can commit to 72 hours in contract language if that is a firm requirement for Medix.
- Subprocessor notifications: we maintain an up-to-date list (attached). For additions we typically notify customers 14 calendar days prior to onboarding; we can discuss a 30-day notification window if you prefer.
- Logging & forensics: Redwood can export request-level logs (timestamp, request id, model, prompt hash, response id) and, where allowed, payloads for a bounded window. Default retention for raw request payloads is 90 days in hosted by default; we offer configurable retention for enterprise/Dedicated including 13 months if required.
- Data residency: we support region pinning (US-East) for production workloads in Dedicated and in-hosted via region selection — we will ensure the addendum captures residency commitments.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.pdf (draft addendum), subprocessor_list_202804.pdf

Proposed next steps:
1) Monica and Karthik will weigh in on a couple of technical/contract tweaks (subprocessor notice window, evidence delivery).
2) I’ll send a consolidated email with suggested language and a DocuSign link for the DPA if that looks good.
3) Can we schedule a 30-minute call Monday to walk legal/procurement through the redline? If Monday is tight, Tuesday morning also works.

If 72h notice is non-negotiable, let me know explicitly and we will prioritize contractual changes.

Thanks — looping in Monica and Karthik for the technical/legal details.

Best,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Post-demo: privacy / DPA clarifications and breach routing

Thanks Mateo — quick technical/ops notes to include in the consolidated response to Medix: 

- KMS & key management: we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys but can integrate with a customer KMS under an enterprise agreement.
- Logs & export format: we can provide event logs (JSON) with request_id, timestamp, model, token counts, and any redaction markers. Full request/response payload export is supported for a customer-specified date range; we typically deliver as gzipped NDJSON. On-demand exports can be produced within 48 hours for a scoped time window (subject to legal/contractual gating).
- Retention defaults & options: hosted default payload retention = 90 days; event metadata retained 365 days. For Dedicated/Private we can configure retention to 13 months or a different SLA — will be captured in the addendum.
- Breach playbook timeline (suggested contractual wording):
  * Detection & triage: 0–24h
  * Internal investigation & containment: 24–72h
  * Customer notification & initial remediation: 72–120h
  * Ongoing remediation & final report: 7–30 days
We can commit to an initial customer notification within 72 hours for confirmed incidents affecting covered data.
- Subprocessor notification: propose two tiers — initial published list included with the DPA; additions announced with at least 30 days' notice for non-critical vendors. For emergency critical patches or urgent infra changes we can include a separate clause allowing shorter notice with post-facto auditability.

Other items: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report via secure link and a copy of our vulnerabilities remediation timeline. For Medix, if they require US-East residency, we should add explicit routing & storage controls into the addendum and include a verification step during onboarding.

I’ve drafted suggested sentence-level language for the subprocessor notice and breach notification windows — happy to paste into the redline if you want.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Apr 2028 09:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy / DPA clarifications and breach routing — next steps

Hi Alicia — thanks again and apologies for the follow-up over the weekend; I wanted to consolidate answers so your procurement/legal team has everything in one place. Below is a short summary plus attachments and next steps.

Summary answers (short):
- Role: Redwood will be listed as Processor in the DPA; we’ll include a mapping table showing the data flow and Medix as Controller.
- 72h breach notice: we will include contractual language committing to written notification within 72 hours of confirmation for incidents affecting Medix production data.
- Subprocessors: attached is our current list. We propose a 30-day notice window for additions (we can accept 14 days if Medix requires shorter). We will add the notification clause to the redline.
- Logs/export: we will provide request-level exports as gzipped NDJSON on request; typical delivery for a scoped export is within 48 hours. Default payload retention = 90 days on hosted, event metadata 365 days; Dedicated customers can request 13 months retention.
- Data residency: US-East region pinning is supported and will be written into the addendum for production workloads.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.pdf, subprocessor_list_202804.pdf

Links: DPA DocuSign (proposed): https://docusign.example.com/signer/abcdef123456
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-54823

Proposed next steps:
1) Review the attached redline. Monica and Karthik have suggested language for the notice windows and evidence delivery — we can incorporate those directly.
2) If the DPA text looks acceptable, I’ll send the DocuSign link and we can aim to complete signatures by May 5 to keep procurement on track.
3) If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call Monday morning (I’m flexible 10–11am ET) to walk legal through the redline.

If you need any clarifications before the call, reply-all and Monica will jump in.

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
